body:
Pushed `2f542760` + `77214101`: a follow-up to the Android Send sheet growth.

With the keyboard still open when a destination resolves (typing a Lightning address, which resolves before you put the keyboard away), the first version rose, dropped by ~320 px and rose again. The Material sheet pads its content by the IME inset, so the full-height column grew a second time as the keyboard left and the animated height lagged behind it. The Send flow now passes its sheet insets without the IME (`CashuModalBottomSheet` gained a `contentWindowInsets` parameter; the input face and the connect-mint URL form pad for the keyboard themselves) and hides the keyboard the moment the input face leaves, so the growth is one motion with the keyboard sliding down beside it.

| Lightning address, keyboard open: first version | keyboard-blind version |
| --- | --- |
| ![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swedishfrenchpress/wallet/qa/layout-jump-audit/docs/qa/layout-jump-audit-2026-10-21/img/pixel-send-lnaddress-keyboard-dip-strip.jpg) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/swedishfrenchpress/wallet/qa/layout-jump-audit/docs/qa/layout-jump-audit-2026-10-21/img/fixed-pixel-send-lnaddress-keyboard-strip.jpg) |

Android unit tests (808), screenshot validation and lint pass on this revision. The test plan (`TESTING.md`, scenario 1) now covers the keyboard-open path and the connect-mint form inside Send.

iOS unit target: 726 passed, 43 skipped, 32 failed without the local mint stack (CDK/Nutshell integration classes); re-running those four classes against the local mints now, result to follow.

iOS unit target result on `77214101`: with the local mint stack up (CDK, Nutshell, payment fixtures and the receipt-recovery proxy), every class passes: 726 passed and 43 skipped without the mints, plus the 77 integration tests that need them (76 passed, 1 skipped). The 32 earlier failures were all the missing-mint classes; none is related to this change.

Pushed `90b2a50e`: the Send sheet's back path (amount face → input) started late and kept sinking after the input face had landed. Two nested size animations were chasing each other: `TwoFaceScreen`'s default `SizeTransform` spring and the "To" row's own height animation kept retargeting the sheet's `animateContentSize`. The face container now snaps its size (the host owns the height), the "To" row changes layout in the same frame as the step and only fades, and the sheet height runs the same 300 ms shared-axis curve as the faces. Measured on the Pixel 7a: the sheet moves on the first frame after the tap and settles with the faces at ~280 ms in both directions. Android unit tests (808), screenshot validation and lint pass; `TESTING.md` scenario 2 updated.
a small one. would appreciate your review @asmogo

**Second pass: ecash and transfer, now stacked on #404.** The branch merges `feat/mint-transfer-capability` (`3d7aa601`), so this PR now shows the transfer commits as well; the two new commits on top are `1d583432` (fixes) and `fa051639` (report + test plan). Report section 9 and `TESTING.md` scenarios 8a–8c and 13–16 cover the new ground: Send Ecash (generate, copy, claimed), Receive → paste → claim page → received, Receive Lightning through the mint picker, and the whole Transfer flow on both platforms. Ten more findings, all with fixes: | | | | |---|---|---| | A12 | Android · Send Ecash | "Checking…" row dropped outright, rows below hop 36 dp | | A13 | Android · Receive | sheet jumps 290 dp to the top in one frame before the keyboard moves | | A14 | Android · Receive | token field grows a line at a time | | A15 | Android · Receive/Send → claim page | keyboard outlives the sheet by ~1 s, then vanishes in one frame | | A16 | Android · Transfer | header chevron pops in/out on Continue/Back | | I7 / I8 | iOS · Send Ecash | token face and "Claimed" face land as cuts | | I9 | iOS · Receive Lightning | I3's invoice landing cuts again on the merged branch (and the paid face on an instant mint) | | I10 | iOS · Add mint | keyboard dropped in one frame while the sheet stays | | I11 | iOS · Receive Lightning | QR greys for one frame when a status poll replaces the quote | The iOS ones share a cause worth knowing about: `sendTokens`, `createMintQuote` and the claim/status checks publish wallet state right before they return, so a `withAnimation` landing in that same run-loop pass renders as a cut. Wrapping alone was not enough (measured); the landings now hop to the next pass first. Transfer itself reads cleanly on both platforms (swap, Max, review, commit, success, back): the chevron pop was its only blemish. iOS, before → after (Send Ecash token face; Receive invoice on the merged branch): **Still to come:** the Pixel 7a filmstrips for A12–A16. The recordings were taken and measured, but the machine rebooted before the strips were cut and the recordings did not survive. A13 and A15 were re-recorded on the fixed build before that and scan as animated; A12, A14 and A16 are marked "fix applied" in the report until the hardware re-check. Android unit tests, screenshot validation and lint pass on the merged branch with the fixes. iOS unit target on the simulator: 893 tests, 871 passed, 0 failed, 22 skipped (local mint fixtures). Side finding, not in scope here: on the Pixel the Send Ecash face never reported a token as claimed although a second wallet redeemed it within a minute (iOS reports it in about six seconds). Worth a separate look at the Android claim probe. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

**Pixel 7a before/after for the second pass is in** (`c19933a9`, `9f0402f3`). Every Android finding was recorded twice with the same script: the merged branch without the fixes, then the fixed build. All five are now verified on hardware; report section 9 has the strips and numbers. One more fix came out of it: animating the sheet column alone (first attempt) eased the sheet's edge while the rows under the token field still hopped a line at a time. The size animation now sits on the Receive and Send destination fields themselves, and the wrap spreads over ~15 frames. A13 Receive sheet on keyboard open, before → after: A15 token handoff (keyboard lingering, then cut), before → after: A14 token wrap, before → after: A12 "Checking…" row and A16 Transfer chevron, after: Also swept on both platforms with nothing to report: Receive → Ecash (new Cashu request page), Send → Tap (Android), Send → paste a token → claim page, Send → Lightning address with the field animation in place, Transfer end to end. One item is left open and documented (I12): the iOS compact Send/Receive sheet steps ~27 pt in one frame when a four-line token is pasted. SwiftUI does not animate a changed `.height` detent even inside `withAnimation` (tried, measured, reverted); the sheet leaves for the claim page within a second, so it is brief. Checks: Android unit tests, screenshot validation and lint pass after the field change; iOS unit target 893 / 871 passed / 0 failed / 22 skipped; no test files changed. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Wallet UI verification Compared `2fbca4a9` with its merge-base `14bde87b` using matched builds from separate clean worktrees, the same synthetic fixtures on both sides, and the environments below. ### Routing - Android: captured — the Send amount step, mint picker, Transfer handoff and destination resolver changed. - iOS: captured — the Send amount step, mint picker, melt keypad note, Transfer handoff and scan/NFC routing changed. ### Capture environments - Android 17 (API 37, build CE2A.260420.019), emulator with a Pixel 10 profile, 1080×2424 at 420 dpi (411 dp wide), dark, en-US, font scale 1.0. - iOS 27.0 (24A434), iPhone 17 Pro simulator, 1206×2622 (402×874 pt at 3×), dark, en-US, Dynamic Type Large; Xcode 27.1 (27A9275). ### Visual findings - Row 1: the inline caution under the To field (which resized the compact sheet) is replaced by the payment sheet's can't-pay face, with the same copy on both platforms and no button. - Row 2: instead of a keypad locked to an empty mint, the face says "Only Lantern Mint can pay invoices without an amount, and it holds 0 sat / ₿0." with a tonal **Transfer to Lantern Mint**. Tapping it opens Transfer with From = Harbor Mint (funded) and To = Lantern Mint (2b). - Row 3: the mint that can't pay is listed last, dimmed, with "Can't pay invoices without an amount". Before, iOS listed only the capable mint and Android offered no picker at all. - Row 4: iOS now dims the amount, shows red "Insufficient balance" and disables Continue. Android is the unchanged control; it already did this. ### Cross-platform parity - Introduced by this change: none observed. Copy, button weight and the Transfer preset match. - Resolved by this change: with one compatible mint, Android offered no picker for an amountless invoice while iOS showed a one-row picker; both now list every mint (row 3). iOS now matches Android's over-balance note (row 4). - Pre-existing, unchanged: the routed sheet's leading control is an X on iOS and a back arrow on Android; these fixtures render amounts as "0 sat" on iOS and "₿0" on Android (₿ symbol setting differs between the fixtures); picker avatars are a generic glyph on iOS and a letter monogram on Android. ### 1. Amountless invoice, no mint can pay one | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | iOS | | | | Android | | | ### 2. Amountless invoice, the only mint that can pay is empty (the reported case) | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | iOS | | | | Android | | | ### 3. Amount keypad, From mint picker (Lantern funded) | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | iOS | | | | Android | | | ### 4. Amount above the From mint's balance (500 typed, 100 held) | | Before | After | |---|---|---| | iOS | | | | Android | | | ### 2b. Transfer opened from the can't-pay face (after only) | iOS | Android | |---|---| | | | Fixture disclosure: two synthetic local CDK FakeWallet mints, "Harbor Mint" (no NUT-05 `amountless`) and "Lantern Mint" (advertises `amountless` through a local proxy that rewrites its `/v1/info`), reached through the repository's payment fixture on iOS. Android uses the androidTest fake gateway with the same mint names, capabilities and balances through a temporary test-only capability override. The invoice is the BOLT #11 specification's amountless example. iOS row 4 used a Lantern-only wallet in a separate run. All capture tests and overrides lived only in the review worktrees. Limitations: static screenshots don't prove Transfer completion, the Pay invoice handoff, NFC or scan behavior; local mints are separate fake Lightning backends, so a cross-mint transfer could not be completed here. Dark mode and default text size only. iOS 27.0 is the newest simulator runtime installed. iOS before rows 1–3 came from the first build of the before revision; the app was re-signed when only the UI-test bundle was rebuilt for row 4.

## Revised compact request sheets

Compared merge-base `14bde87b` with `e44493f2` on both native apps. **Before** is the original implementation; **after** is the revised compact shared view.

Receive and History now use the same content-sized request sheet, with a drag handle and no redundant leading close/back control. Addresses and reusable invoices retain one trailing Share/New menu. Android's Details alignment is corrected. Completed receipts retain their presentation.

- iOS 26.5 / 23F77 (approved installed-runtime fallback); iPhone 17 Pro profile, 1206×2622, Xcode 26.6 / 17F113.
- Light appearance, English US, normal text. All 28 PNGs passed manifest validation and visual inspection.

**Fixture disclosure:** synthetic mint, quotes, invoices and completed receipt only. Android exercised normal navigation with a fake gateway; iOS presented production views through a temporary debug fixture host with reset request storage and frozen network refresh. The original before captures were reused unchanged from the validated baseline. Capture adapters are not included in the PR.

**Validation:** three Android capture journeys and the on-chain History regression passed. The iOS seven-surface capture journey passed, including native drag dismissal for active requests. Native typography, icon orientation and date formatting differ; Android system status-bar positioning is capture noise. No new cross-platform action gap was observed in these states.

**Limits:** screenshots do not prove real payments, NFC, background behavior or accessibility announcements. Dark mode, large text, physical devices, current-stable iOS, expired/missing quotes and funded reusable requests were not captured. Synthetic regtest addresses omit explorer links.

## Wallet UI verification

I compared this PR with its merge base (`fba0ccc6` → `c8ed5464`) using clean Debug builds from separate worktrees, on the same simulator, driven by the same UI test.

### Routing

- Android: skipped. No compiled Android app input changed.
- iOS: captured. `AmountLockup` and `CurrencyAmountDisplay` changed.

### Capture environment

- iPhone 17 Pro simulator, iOS 27.0 (24A434), Xcode 27.1 (27A9275), 1206×2622 px @3x, dark, en-US, Large text.

### Visual findings

- **Typing 210 → 2,100:** before, the 2 and the trailing 0 hold still while the 1 rolls out and back in and a 0 rolls in after it. After, the typed 0 comes in at the right end, 210 slides left and the comma blurs in between the 2 and the 1.
- **At rest:** no visible change. Only the amount line's pixels differ: glyphs sit up to 2 px apart per digit, 3 px at `sat`, at 3×. Everything else on screen is pixel-identical.

Fixture disclosure: two local FakeWallet CDK mints with synthetic names (Alpine Mint, Harbor Mint), and a fresh wallet funded with 21,000 synthetic sats. A temporary UI test, identical in both worktrees and removed afterwards, typed 2-1-0-0 at a fixed pace.

Limitations:
- The keystroke frames are sampled from a `simctl recordVideo` capture (H.264, retimed by decode timestamps), not screenshots. The settled images are XCUITest screenshots.
- Not covered: other text sizes, light appearance, fiat entry, and amounts long enough to need scaling.

## Wallet UI verification

Compared `b883a07f` with its merge-base `001cd8d7` using matched clean builds. Both sides of each pair ran the same steps from the same fixture.

### Routing

- Android: captured. The home balance, Recent rows and History rows changed.
- iOS: captured. The same surfaces changed.

### Capture environments

- Android 17 (API 37, CE2A.260420.019), Pixel 6 profile, 1080×2400 px at 420 dpi, dark, en-US, font scale 1.0.
- iOS 27.0 (24A434), Xcode 27.1, iPhone 18 Pro, 1206×2622 px (402×874 pt @3x), dark, en-US, Dynamic Type Large.

### Visual findings

- **At launch, nothing changes.** The iOS pair is byte-identical. The Android pair differs only in the status-bar noise noted below.
- **Second tap on the balance:** on `main` it returns to bitcoin. Here it reaches private:
  - the balance shows `****` with no unit, centred where the digits were;
  - the fiat line empties but keeps its slot, so Receive/Send and the rows below don't move;
  - Recent rows show `****` with no sign, green for receipts and white for sends.
- **Android's hidden balance** is set one weight lighter than the digits, because Geist's asterisk is heavier than SF's. The two platforms' `****` now look about the same weight.
- **History** masks the same way. Rows keep their colour but drop the sign, and the fiat lines keep their height.
- Both apps hide the same things the same way.

### Home, as launched

## Wallet UI verification

Compared `841a472531d6a5579b183f500f768d67524ca8a4` with its actual merge-base `14bde87b9a25ef9f14558e913301083c3d6b3f48` using isolated instrumented builds and matched before/after environments. **23 pairs / 46 screenshots: 22 Android and 24 iOS.** Both platforms were routed because their compiled views changed.

### Findings

- **P3 — iOS Details chevron wraps below its label at accessibility text sizes.** [PaymentDetailsButton](https://github.com/cashubtc/wallet/blob/841a472531d6a5579b183f500f768d67524ca8a4/ios/CashuWallet/Views/Components/PaymentDetailContent.swift#L137-L142) uses the same stacking layout as metadata values. This puts the disclosure chevron on a second line in the address and completed-receipt screens; Android keeps it trailing on the same line. This is introduced by the PR. Recommend keeping the Details label and chevron together while retaining stacked metadata values.
- **Large-text action placement differs:** Android keeps Copy address pinned; iOS puts Copy Address below the initial viewport. The supplemental native UI check confirms it is hittable after scrolling on both iOS revisions. This is a visible parity difference, not an inaccessible action.
- The earlier **Android Details inset/alignment issue is resolved**. No additional foreground rendering regression was observed in the normal-size or dark captures.

### Surface results

| Surface | Result |
|---|---|
| Address from Receive and History | Shared compact QR/metadata presentation; status, address, mint, creation data and copy action retained. History sharing moves into the overflow menu. |
| Address technical Details | Transaction facts, quote ID and request retained within each platform. |
| Reusable invoice from Receive and History | Shared editable Amount and Details presentation; Android's old History-only NFC-unavailable banner disappears. NFC behavior was not tested. |
| Unpaid Lightning History | Shared compact invoice; amount and mint remain prominent. Pending and date move into technical Details. |
| Completed receipt | Paid state, amount, date, mint and payment proof retained; no actionable QR. iOS large text now stacks readonly metadata, improving parity except for the chevron issue. |
| Dark appearance | Readable metadata/actions and white QR background retained. |

Other differences are pre-existing native conventions: copy-label capitalization, overflow-menu orientation, date formatting, sheet styling and dismissal behavior. The technical inspector's extra Android quote-snapshot rows are a fixture-coverage difference, not evidence of a product regression. No other action/content divergence was observed in the paired surfaces.

### Capture environments

- **Android:** Android 17 / API 37, build CE2A.260420.019 / 15611780, arm64, security patch 2026-05-05; Pixel 7 profile, 1080×2400, 420 dpi; light/dark; en-US; font scale 1.0 and 2.0.
- **iOS:** iOS 26.5 / 23F77, Xcode 26.6 / 17F113; iPhone 17 Pro, 1206×2622, 402×874 points at 3×; light/dark; en-US; Dynamic Type Large and Accessibility Large. The installed iOS 26.5 fallback was explicitly approved; iOS 27 is not covered.
- Exact same OS image/device for each before/after pair; fixed synthetic creation time and status-bar clock. Native large-text categories are semantically comparable rather than identical pixel multipliers. No availability or deployment-target boundary changed.
